title: Short-term interruption versus continuous anticoagulation in colorectal polypectomy. A randomized multicenter investigator-initiated non-inferiority clinical trial: the POLYPHEM trial.
official: Short-term interruption versus continuous anticoagulation in colorectal polypectomy. A randomized multicenter investigator-initiated non-inferiority clinical trial: the POLYPHEM trial.
summary: Main objective: To evaluate the safety of maintaining anticoagulationtratment during polypectomy in colorrectal lesions.
conditions: Patients receiving oral anticoagulant therapy who are scheduled for elective colonoscopy for any indication.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Age 18 years or older
2. Patients undergoing elective outpatient colonoscopy for any indication
3. Anticoagulant treatment with VKA (acenocoumarol or warfarin) or OACD (dabigatran, edoxaban, apixaban or rivaroxaban) prior to colonoscopy
Exclusion criteria:
1. Concomitant antiagregant treatment
2. Planned endoscopic dilatation
3. Severe psychiatric disorder
4. Removal of colorectal lesion by endoscopic submucosal dissection
5. Previous diagnosis of renal failure defined as creatinine >2 mg/dl or clearance < 30 ml/min
6. Planned procedure of high haemorrhagic risk in simultaneously performed gastroscopy
7. Prior trial enrolment. Patients may only be included on one occasion
8. Any clinical situation or concomitant treatment that in the investigator's judgement poses a significant bleeding risk
9. Age > 85 years old
10. Urgent colonoscopy
11. Labile INR (time in therapeutic range less than 60%) documented in the previous 3 months in patients receiving VKAs
12. Supra-therapeutic INR (> 3.5) at the time of the procedure in patients receiving VKA
13. Pregnancy
14. Decompensated liver cirrhosis
15. Inability, in the investigator's judgement, to understand the periprocedural anticoagulation regimen
16. Previously known coagulopathy or bleeding diathesis. Includes plateletopenia < 50,000/µL in the previous 12 months
